text: What is the fundamental problem of an economy?
options: What to produce?
How to produce?
For whom to produce?
All of the above
explanation: An economy faces three fundamental problems: what to produce, how to produce, and for whom to produce. These problems are central to the functioning of an economy.
subject: Economics

text: Which of the following is a characteristic of a scarcity?
options: Abundance of resources
Insufficient resources
Perfectly elastic demand
Perfectly inelastic supply
explanation: Scarcity refers to the insufficiency of resources to meet the unlimited wants of individuals. It is a fundamental problem of an economy.
subject: Economics

text: What is the opportunity cost of producing one more unit of a good?
options: Marginal Benefit
Marginal Cost
Marginal Revenue
Marginal Opportunity Cost
explanation: Opportunity cost refers to the next best alternative that is given up when a choice is made. Marginal opportunity cost is the opportunity cost of producing one more unit of a good.
subject: Economics

text: What is the Production Possibility Curve (PPC)?
options: A curve that shows the maximum possible output of two goods
A curve that shows the minimum possible output of two goods
A curve that shows the equilibrium price of two goods
A curve that shows the equilibrium quantity of two goods
correctAnswer: A curve that shows the maximum possible output of two goods
explanation: The Production Possibility Curve (PPC) is a graphical representation of the maximum possible output of two goods that can be produced with the given resources and technology.
subject: Economics

text: What is the relationship between the Marginal Opportunity Cost (MOC) and the Production Possibility Curve (PPC)?
options: MOC is equal to the slope of the PPC
MOC is equal to the intercept of the PPC
MOC is equal to the distance between the PPC and the origin
MOC is equal to the distance between the PPC and the axes
correctAnswer: MOC is equal to the slope of the PPC
explanation: The Marginal Opportunity Cost (MOC) is equal to the slope of the Production Possibility Curve (PPC). It represents the rate at which the opportunity cost of producing one more unit of a good increases.
subject: Economics

text: What is the difference between Positive Economics and Normative Economics?
options: Positive Economics deals with what is, while Normative Economics deals with what ought to be
Positive Economics deals with what ought to be, while Normative Economics deals with what is
Positive Economics deals with the causes of economic phenomena, while Normative Economics deals with the effects of economic phenomena
Positive Economics deals with the effects of economic phenomena, while Normative Economics deals with the causes of economic phenomena
correctAnswer: Positive Economics deals with what is, while Normative Economics deals with what ought to be
explanation: Positive Economics deals with the description and analysis of economic phenomena, while Normative Economics deals with the evaluation and prescription of economic policies.
subject: Economics

text: What is the concept of Opportunity Cost?
options: The cost of producing a good or service
The benefit of producing a good or service
The next best alternative that is given up when a choice is made
The cost of not producing a good or service
correctAnswer: The next best alternative that is given up when a choice is made
explanation: Opportunity cost refers to the next best alternative that is given up when a choice is made. It is the cost of choosing one option over another.
